models.collectorNote: The Bond premium is real and permanent. Matching numbers and a known history matter more than colour; the Vantage-spec cars are the blue-chip end.

generations.name: DB5
generations.note: 4.0 litres, triple SUs or Webers in the Vantage, 145 mph. Just over a thousand built, including the film cars that made it the most recognised Aston Martin on Earth.

models.intro: The Goldfinger car, though the DB4 did the engineering, the DB5 did the immortality. Tadek Marek's twin-cam six, a ZF five-speed, and the template for every Aston since.
models.name: DB5

photos.credit: Photo: Calreyn88, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

models.collectorNote: Manual 4.7s and any V12 Vantage are the holds. Budget for clutch and subframe corrosion checks, the cars reward owners who use specialists.

generations.name: V8 Vantage (4.3)
generations.note: Launched as the 'baby Aston' against the 911 Carrera, bonded aluminium VH chassis, dry-sump V8 behind the front axle line.

generations.name: V8 Vantage (4.7) / V12 Vantage
generations.note: The 4.7 fixed the torque curve; the V12 Vantage S of 2013 stuffed the DBS's 5.9 V12 into the smallest Aston and created the connoisseur's pick of the whole range.

models.intro: The Gaydon-era entry Aston: hand-assembled Jaguar-derived V8, a proper manual gearbox for most of its life, and styling that aged better than anything else in its class.
models.name: V8 Vantage

generations.name: DB11 V12
generations.note: The 5.2 twin-turbo V12 was developed in-house with AMG electronics. Aerodynamic 'curlicue' ducts in the C-pillars did the work of a spoiler.

generations.name: DB11 V8 / AMR
generations.note: The Mercedes-AMG 4.0 V8 dropped 115 kg over the front axle. The AMR of 2018 sharpened the V12 car to 630 hp before the DB12 replaced the line.

models.intro: The first car of Aston's 'second century' plan: new bonded structure, a twin-turbo V12 of Aston's own, then an AMG V8 that many testers preferred for its lighter nose.
models.name: DB11

generations.name: DBX / DBX707
generations.note: AMG's 4.0 V8 in two tunes; the 707 (697 hp) added a wet-clutch nine-speed and bigger turbos. Air suspension keeps the GT brief credible on real roads.

models.intro: The SUV that saved Aston Martin, built in a new Welsh factory. The DBX707 briefly held the title of most powerful production SUV in the world.
models.name: DBX

models.collectorNote: There is no casual Valkyrie market, cars trade privately at multiples of list. Provenance is everything; most will live in collections, not on roads.

generations.name: Valkyrie / AMR Pro
generations.note: The brief was a 1:1 power-to-weight ratio in kilograms and horsepower, and it got there. The track-only AMR Pro drops the hybrid and the road equipment, not the ambition.

models.intro: Adrian Newey's road car: a Cosworth V12 revving to 11,000 rpm, a hybrid system filling the torque gaps, and downforce figures from a Formula 1 wind tunnel. 150 coupés, all spoken for.
models.name: Valkyrie
